hook.text: A peacock's giant tail is useless for survival. That's the point—only a fit bird can afford the handicap.

buildup.text: Signaling means conveying hidden information through costly, hard-to-fake actions.

discovery.text: Michael Spence won a Nobel for showing how education works as a signal even if it teaches nothing practical.

twist.text: The signal must be costly to be credible. Cheap signals—like simply claiming you're great—convince nobody.

climax.text: Warranties, luxury brands, and engagement rings all work because they cost more than a liar would pay.

punchline.text: What you sacrifice says more than what you say.

quiz.question: Why must signals be costly to be credible?
options: Because expensive things are always better
Because cheap signals can be easily faked
Because cost is irrelevant to signaling
